articles.expand: The headline beat should support the Australian dollar and short-dated yields at the margin, as traders reassess how firmly they had ruled out another RBA hike. The detail limits the hawkish case, though. Private sector strength came from a one-off award decision, public sector pay is doing much of the work, and real wages are still falling, so it’s hard to argue wages are driving inflation. That mix makes a large repricing of December less likely. articles.expand: On balance the minutes lean hawkish, unsurpisngly. The majority’s view that 4.85% is “not clearly sufficient” sits awkwardly with market pricing that had all but ruled out further hikes, and it backs up Bullock’s comment this morning about upside risks. The minority’s warning of a sharper downturn sets a high bar for a December move, though. This week’s wage and jobs data, and the October CPI jump the staff flagged in advance, matter more than usual. articles.title: RBA’s Bullock says inflation risks still skewed to upside ahead of 6-3 vote minutes
articles.expand: Bullock’s comment pushes back modestly against market pricing that has all but ruled out a December hike. It could offer the Australian dollar some support after it fell this week to its lowest level since late January. One line on a panel is unlikely to shift pricing on its own, so the minutes are the bigger test. Any sign that the majority on the board saw a real chance of further tightening would firm up the hawkish reading of Bullock’s remarks. If the minutes play up how close the vote was, front-end rates may decide the governor’s comment is a hedge, not a signal. - Minutes preview here: ...
